newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Jiang hails new ideology watchdog.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang hails new ideology watchdog.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Monday hailed a powerful new ideological watchdog body headed by a hardliner as essential to the future of China's people and its ruling Communist Party.

The Central Leading Committee for Construction of Spiritual Civilisation would oversee the carrying out of party decrees on building "spiritual civilisation" -- party jargon for socialist ethics, the official Xinhua news agency said.

"Developing socialist spiritual civilisation is related to the fate and prospects of the party and the nation and to the Chinese people proudly... towering among the peoples of the world," Xinhua quoted Jiang as telling the committee's opening session.
The committee would be headed by Ding Guangen, Xinhua said.

Jiang has promoted "spiritual civilisation" as a way to revive communist doctrines of civic responsibility and self-sacrifice as many officials worry that nearly two decades of capitalist-style economic reforms have eroded traditional Marxist values.
"The history of human society has shown that a people must not be materially poor, nor should they be spiritually poor," Xinhua quoted Jiang as saying.
"Only by being rich both materially and spiritually can they become a people full of strong vitality and cohesiveness," Jiang said.

Chinese sources said last week the appointment of Ding, head of the Propaganda Department of the party's Central Committee, was a signal that the star of the protege of late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping was on the rise.
The Leading Committee for Construction of Spiritual Civilisation is a more powerful body than the Propaganda Department.

Such leading groups are policy-making bodies often headed by members of the Politburo Standing Committee, and Ding's appointment signalled he could join that omnipotent body at the 15th party congress later this year, the sources said.

But Jiang made clear that creation of the group did not mark a deviation from the pragmatic economic policies set in place by his mentor Deng Xiaoping, who died in February and whose shoes Jiang has been left to fill.

"Work on construction of spiritual civilisation must serve economic construction and must serve modernisation," he said. "The basic task of socialism is to liberate and develop the forces of production."
Instilling proper values was imperative to ensuring China's continued economic growth, Jiang said.

"If construction of spiritual civilisation is not done well, the people's hearts will sap, spirits will turn decadent and it will be difficult to do a good job with economic construction and other matters," he said.

Ding, a former favoured bridge partner of Deng Xiaoping, who died on February 19, aged 92, is known for his openly hardline approach and last year urged that social science research should stress Marxism and Mao Zedong thought.
Ding has tightened the party's iron grip on the media in recent years, bringing down the ideological axe on many books, movies and arts events since he took over the propaganda reins in 1992.
